scene.label: Act 1, Scene 2
scene.title: SCENE II. Paris. A room in the King's palace.
scene.location: Paris. A room in the King's palace.

content.text: Flourish of cornets. Enter the King of France, with letters; Lords and others attending.

lines.text: The Florentines and Senoys are by th' ears;
lines.plainText: The Florentines and Senoys are by th' ears

lines.text: Have fought with equal fortune, and continue
lines.plainText: Have fought with equal fortune and continue

lines.text: A braving war.
lines.plainText: A braving war

lines.text: So 'tis reported, sir.
lines.plainText: So 'tis reported sir

lines.text: Nay, 'tis most credible, we here receive it,
lines.plainText: Nay 'tis most credible we here receive it

lines.text: A certainty, vouch'd from our cousin Austria,
lines.plainText: A certainty vouch'd from our cousin Austria

lines.text: With caution, that the Florentine will move us
lines.plainText: With caution that the Florentine will move us

lines.text: For speedy aid; wherein our dearest friend
lines.plainText: For speedy aid wherein our dearest friend

lines.text: Prejudicates the business, and would seem
lines.plainText: Prejudicates the business and would seem

lines.text: To have us make denial.
lines.plainText: To have us make denial

lines.text: His love and wisdom,
lines.plainText: His love and wisdom

lines.plainText: Approv'd so to your majesty may plead

lines.text: For amplest credence.
lines.plainText: For amplest credence

lines.plainText: He hath arm'd our answer

lines.plainText: And Florence is denied before he comes

lines.plainText: Yet for our gentlemen that mean to see

lines.plainText: The Tuscan service freely have they leave

lines.text: To stand on either part.

lines.plainText: It well may serve

lines.text: For breathing and exploit.
lines.plainText: For breathing and exploit

lines.text: What's he comes here?
lines.plainText: What's he comes here

lines.text: It is the Count Rossillon, my good lord,
lines.plainText: It is the Count Rossillon my good lord

lines.text: Young Bertram.
lines.plainText: Young Bertram

lines.text: Youth, thou bear'st thy father's face;
lines.plainText: Youth thou bear'st thy father's face

lines.text: Frank nature, rather curious than in haste,
lines.plainText: Frank nature rather curious than in haste

lines.text: Hath well compos'd thee. Thy father's moral parts
lines.plainText: Hath well compos'd thee Thy father's moral parts

lines.text: Mayst thou inherit too! Welcome to Paris.
lines.plainText: Mayst thou inherit too Welcome to Paris

lines.text: My thanks and duty are your majesty's.
lines.plainText: My thanks and duty are your majesty's

lines.text: I would I had that corporal soundness now,
lines.plainText: I would I had that corporal soundness now

lines.text: As when thy father and myself in friendship
lines.plainText: As when thy father and myself in friendship

lines.text: First tried our soldiership. He did look far
lines.plainText: First tried our soldiership He did look far

lines.text: Into the service of the time, and was
lines.plainText: Into the service of the time and was

lines.text: Discipled of the bravest. He lasted long,
lines.plainText: Discipled of the bravest He lasted long

lines.text: But on us both did haggish age steal on,
lines.plainText: But on us both did haggish age steal on

lines.text: And wore us out of act. It much repairs me
lines.plainText: And wore us out of act It much repairs me

lines.text: To talk of your good father; in his youth
lines.plainText: To talk of your good father in his youth

lines.text: He had the wit which I can well observe
lines.plainText: He had the wit which I can well observe

lines.text: Today in our young lords; but they may jest
lines.plainText: Today in our young lords but they may jest

lines.text: Till their own scorn return to them unnoted
lines.plainText: Till their own scorn return to them unnoted

lines.text: Ere they can hide their levity in honour
lines.plainText: Ere they can hide their levity in honour

lines.text: So like a courtier, contempt nor bitterness
lines.plainText: So like a courtier contempt nor bitterness

lines.text: Were in his pride or sharpness; if they were,
lines.plainText: Were in his pride or sharpness if they were

lines.text: His equal had awak'd them, and his honour,
lines.plainText: His equal had awak'd them and his honour

lines.text: Clock to itself, knew the true minute when
lines.plainText: Clock to itself knew the true minute when

lines.plainText: Exception bid him speak and at this time

lines.plainText: His tongue obey'd his hand Who were below him

lines.plainText: He us'd as creatures of another place

lines.plainText: And bow'd his eminent top to their low ranks

lines.text: Making them proud of his humility,
lines.plainText: Making them proud of his humility

lines.plainText: In their poor praise he humbled Such a man

lines.text: Might be a copy to these younger times;
lines.plainText: Might be a copy to these younger times

lines.plainText: But goers backward

lines.plainText: His good remembrance sir

lines.plainText: Lies richer in your thoughts than on his tomb

lines.text: So in approof lives not his epitaph
lines.plainText: So in approof lives not his epitaph

lines.text: As in your royal speech.
lines.plainText: As in your royal speech

lines.text: Would I were with him! He would always say,—
lines.plainText: Would I were with him He would always say

lines.text: Methinks I hear him now; his plausive words
lines.plainText: Methinks I hear him now his plausive words

lines.text: He scatter'd not in ears, but grafted them
lines.plainText: He scatter'd not in ears but grafted them

lines.text: To grow there and to bear,—"Let me not live,"
lines.plainText: To grow there and to bearLet me not live

lines.text: This his good melancholy oft began
lines.plainText: This his good melancholy oft began

lines.text: On the catastrophe and heel of pastime,
lines.plainText: On the catastrophe and heel of pastime

lines.plainText: When it was outLet me not live quoth he

lines.plainText: After my flame lacks oil to be the snuff

lines.text: Of younger spirits, whose apprehensive senses
lines.plainText: Of younger spirits whose apprehensive senses

lines.text: All but new things disdain; whose judgments are
lines.plainText: All but new things disdain whose judgments are

lines.plainText: Mere fathers of their garments whose constancies

lines.text: Expire before their fashions." This he wish'd.
lines.plainText: Expire before their fashions This he wish'd

lines.text: I, after him, do after him wish too,
lines.plainText: I after him do after him wish too

lines.text: Since I nor wax nor honey can bring home,
lines.plainText: Since I nor wax nor honey can bring home

lines.text: I quickly were dissolved from my hive
lines.plainText: I quickly were dissolved from my hive

lines.text: To give some labourers room.
lines.plainText: To give some labourers room

lines.text: You're lov'd, sir;
lines.plainText: You're lov'd sir

lines.text: They that least lend it you shall lack you first.
lines.plainText: They that least lend it you shall lack you first

lines.text: I fill a place, I know't. How long is't, Count,
lines.plainText: I fill a place I know't How long is't Count

lines.text: Since the physician at your father's died?
lines.plainText: Since the physician at your father's died

lines.text: He was much fam'd.
lines.plainText: He was much fam'd

lines.plainText: Some six months since my lord

lines.text: If he were living, I would try him yet;—
lines.plainText: If he were living I would try him yet

lines.text: Lend me an arm;—the rest have worn me out
lines.plainText: Lend me an armthe rest have worn me out

lines.text: With several applications; nature and sickness
lines.plainText: With several applications nature and sickness

lines.text: Debate it at their leisure. Welcome, Count;
lines.plainText: Debate it at their leisure Welcome Count

lines.text: My son's no dearer.
lines.plainText: My son's no dearer
